entry.title: Bradford Cox Surprise-Releases Thanatos, Atlas Sound’s First New Album In 15 Years
entry.summary: Finally, suddenly, we have a whole new album from Bradford Cox. After reviving his solo project Atlas Sound for a performance at Philadelphia’s Making Time ∞ festival in September and sharing the comeback single “Octoberland” in October, Cox has released the new full-length Thanatos. It’s his first album of any kind since Deerhunter’s Why Hasn’t…
entry.content:
Finally, suddenly, we have a whole new album from Bradford Cox. After reviving his solo project Atlas Sound for a performance at Philadelphia's Making Time ∞ festival in September and sharing the comeback single "Octoberland" in October, Cox has released the new full-length Thanatos. It's his first album of any kind since Deerhunter's Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared? in 2019 and the first Atlas Sound album since Parallax in 2011.

Thanatos includes 10 songs, most of which Cox performed at Making Time ∞. He recorded the album alone in his attic in Atlanta's Grant Park neighborhood with a Tascam DP-008, a portable 8-track recorder. It's billed as the completion of a trilogy with 2009's Logos and 2011's Parallax. (Sorry to 2008's Let The Blind Lead Those Who See But Cannot Feel — you're on your own.) Heba Kadry mastered the recordings, Chris Reynolds made the sculpture on the album cover, Javier Morales did the photography, and Cox's late dog Faulkner is credited with emotional support.

Thanatos is digital-only for now but will be available on vinyl next year. Sign up at Atlas Sound's website for updates on that. The album comes with a hand-scribbled "scent map" assigning smells to each of the 10 tracks, a video called "A Visit With Bradford Cox," and a biography from Cox's longtime friend and collaborator Cate Le Bon. Sift through all that below while you stream Thanatos.

Here is Le Bon's bio:

Bradford Cox has always existed in extremes.

Embracing and transcending the contradictions inherent in an artist reaching for all the corners.

Impossible to capture or imitate.

Here,

is he dissolving the boundary between death and rebirth?

Something irreversible is happening.

Rupture and renewal.

Virginia Woolf accessed her enormous eye by leaving the house.

Bradford Cox finds it by burrowing deeper inside the familiar shell that is his home. Sheltered from all exterior weather fronts. surrounded by objects he has collected and absorbed for decades and held by the warmth of the love of his life. He has
consumed it all and transformed geometrical space into a living burial chamber where he can shed the self. He works only in the dead of night.

Minimal interruptions and ritualistic scene setting allows for subconscious nocturnal abandon that yields this music of growth, destruction, renewal and cessation.

Each vocal take is a performance.

Each instrument played like it’s his last night on earth.

That could always be true. Without this awareness of mortality; love, passion and creation lose substance.

The Tascam, a tool to distil the process down to the fundamentals of subtraction and addition. The former a by-product of the latter. Nothing deleted but instead painted over with new emotion or the same gesture repeated with the urgency of the
moment. He is somehow capturing the impermanence of a waterfall without making it concrete.

Lyrically led by a disassociated primordial wisdom usually found in the sediment of dreams. A feeling you cannot name but it scratches at the heart and soul. Elusive but knowable. It is the past sung without memory of it but evoked by an action, a
gesture, a ritual, a will. A means to access and revise an incomprehensible truth that you slept without knowing a loved one once.

It is alive,

human.

Complicated and lucid.

It understands the difference between knowing and realising something elemental.

For my part / To me, at least.

It is everything I want from him

and nothing I expected.

Cate Le Bon

entry.title: Bloom And Ruin (Efrim Manuel Menuck & Tashi Dorji) Announce New Album Two Liberations 2
entry.summary: Bloom And Ruin brings together two of our greatest living noise-makers: Efrim Manuel Menuck, the Montreal musician behind the brilliant post-rock bands Godspeed You! Black Emperor and Thee Silver Mt. Zion Memorial Orchestra, and Tashi Dorji, the Bhutanese-born, Asheville-based experimental guitarist. They released their debut album Two Liberations in the spring, and they’re back today…
entry.content:
Bloom And Ruin brings together two of our greatest living noise-makers: Efrim Manuel Menuck, the Montreal musician behind the brilliant post-rock bands Godspeed You! Black Emperor and Thee Silver Mt. Zion Memorial Orchestra, and Tashi Dorji, the Bhutanese-born, Asheville-based experimental guitarist. They released their debut album Two Liberations in the spring, and they're back today with news of a sequel, as well as an extensive 2027 tour.

Like its predecessor, Two Liberations 2 comprises two lengthy improvisations. They recorded it at Ritual Botanica, an herbal apothecary near Dorji's Asheville home. A friend named Potions oversaw the sessions. The new album's second track, "Kids Free (As They Should Be)," is streaming now. If you're into Godspeed's ominous droning triumph, you'll love this. I also appreciate that it's paired with a song called "Workers Take The Building." In a press release, the duo offers this statement: "The work is part lament, part rallying cry, part ritual... the combination yielding a triumphant, spectral protest."

It's a spotlight moment for Menuck, who has mostly moved in the shadows throughout his decades of music-making. Last week Hearing Things published a lengthy feature billed as the first-ever GY!BE profile, reported by the prolific Grayson Haver Currin. It's available now in audio form too if you subscribe over there. I wonder how it sounds overlaid with "Kids Free (As They Should Be)." Only one way to find out...

entry.title: Spencer Zahn Announces New Album Heart: Hear “tearless”
entry.summary: Composer Spencer Zahn has announced the solo fretless bass album 'Heart' and shared its lovely lead single "tearless."
entry.content:
The only instrument that composer Spencer Zahn brought with him when he moved to Los Angeles in 2023 was a 1970s Fender Precision fretless electric bass, and it quickly became his signature sound. After his longtime collaborator Dave Harrington asked him to come up with a solo fretless bass set to open for Darkside, he decided to record an entire album exploring the possibilities of the instrument.

That album, Heart, will be out in February. The title is "a reminder to stay true to myself in the musical process and in life," Zahn explains. And although he's released solo albums in addition to his work with artists like Dawn Richard and Joseph Shabason, he says that "in many ways, this feels like my debut album." Its harmonics-laden opener and lead single "tearless" is warm and lovely, continuing Zahn's ongoing dedication to collapsing the difference between classical, jazz, ambient, and pop music.

"'tearless'' was the first song I recorded when beginning work on the album," Zahn says. "I had been playing around with the idea of a solo fretless bass record for a few months and was trying versions of this song on tour. One day it started to fit together into this final form which also gave shape and a solid direction for the rest of the music. It's only fretless bass but sounds like lots of instruments. I wanted it to feel like walking into a room and discovering all the small details one by one." Listen below.

Heart is out 2/5 via Western Vinyl. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: Beabadoobee Announces New Album Bananas 4 Cats: Hear “No Punctuation”
entry.summary: Beabadoobee isn’t wasting any time this year. Today, only two months after the release of her chart-topping Pylon, the British alt-pop musician announced a new album called Bananas 4 Cats. The new album isn’t really a new chapter for Bea Laus, but a shift in perspective. Whereas Pylon was made on the road with a…
entry.content:
Beabadoobee isn't wasting any time this year. Today, only two months after the release of her chart-topping Pylon, the British alt-pop musician announced a new album called Bananas 4 Cats. The new album isn't really a new chapter for Bea Laus, but a shift in perspective. Whereas Pylon was made on the road with a list of stellar collaborators like Hayley Williams and Deftones' Chino Moreno, Bananas 4 Cats was written and recorded in her East London home with her friends and her cats.

“I just needed to write an album like this after Pylon. It happened naturally, I got back home and felt inspired, and made another album,” she said in a press release.

Bananas 4 Cats is out in February and contains 14 tracks, though no tracklist has yet been released. The first single, out now, is "No Punctuation," which fans might recognize. It's a song that Bea has been playing live over the years and has circulated online. And if you think Bea and her team weren't doing anything fun given that album title, think again! You can now pre-order vinyl that features banana-scented artwork.

Listen to "No Punctuation" below.

entry.title: Take A Ride On JW Francis’ Route 66
entry.summary: Remember when things were simpler? Felt kinder and less hostile? When you didn’t have to worry about productivity-maxxing or getting suckered with AI-created ads? I love music that reminds me all I have to do is exist. The latest project to do that for me is Route 66, the liberating new album from the formerly…
entry.content:
Remember when things were simpler? Felt kinder and less hostile? When you didn't have to worry about productivity-maxxing or getting suckered with AI-created ads? I love music that reminds me all I have to do is exist. The latest project to do that for me is Route 66, the liberating new album from the formerly NYC-based musician JW Francis, who moved to LA last year and lives in an RV. It's such a feel good vibe, man — like hopping into your car after a work shift when the sun is shining and life feels full of possibility.

Aside from the fuzzy, chillaxed vocals (which at times makes Francis sound like Mac DeMarco or Kurt Vile) and wanderlust-filled lyrics, Route 66 is a wholesome project. Raised in Sapulpa, OK, Francis grew up close to the famous highway. The album samples his grandmother and features artwork made by his father. It was also certified as a National Route 66 Centennial Certified Project.

Francis is an adventurous soul, too. Not only is he a prolific musician, he's also a dedicated traveller, with a knack for taking on ambitious journeys that fuel his creative output. He completed his ode to Route 66 by traveling the full length of the famous highway. It follows two albums inspired by his previous expeditions: canoeing the length of the Mississippi River and hiking the Appalachian Trail. A spirit of curiosity and freedom runs right through his work.

In an Instagram post, Francis shared that: "Route 66 is the end of a trilogy of adventure albums. Not that I'm done adventuring, but my first three albums were largely about New York, the next three about American corridors. What comes next, I don't know, but what connects it all is LOVE!!!"

Listen to Route 66 below.

Route 66 is out now.

entry.content:
Caspian Hollywell, frontman for the ascendant New Orleans rock band Twisted Teens, was accused of being an "abuser" and a "rapist defender" on flyers anonymously posted around his home base of New Orleans last weekend. Hollywell (above right) denied the allegations in an Instagram story posted from the band's account Wednesday night.

The flyers read as follows:

FUCK TWISTED TEENS!
Caspian is an abuser, rapist defender, entitled nepo baby cosplaying as a blue collar new orleans punk. He grew up in Marin California. His parents are multi-millionaires. Mommy and Daddy bought his house in the lower ninth. He has never had to work a day in his life. He is a thief and a fraud.
Caspian's close friend kidnapped, repeatedly raped and threatened to murder a community member in santa cruz. Caspian covered it up, housed her abuser, ostracized and alienated her, told everyone she was crazy and a liar, and terrorized her for years. She lives with PTSD to this day.
This is just one example. There is much much more. This is a call to action!! If you support women, care about your community or music scene - publicly shame subpop, pitchfork, kurt vile, and anyone else who gives this disgusting man a platform!
We are many, we are strong, our numbers grow by the day and our voices will be heard! The truth will come out. We will not stop until Caspian is exposed for what he is. To the women he has abused, we see you, we love you, you are not alone.
EAT THE FUCKING RICH

Here's Hollywell's response:

A person I've never met in my life has been putting flyers around New Orleans w/ some pretty intense accusations against me, and then reposting it far and wide on the internet.

The extreme events the flyers refer to is not something I recognize and seems to be coming from someone who is a total stranger. I've spent the last couple of days frantically combing through my past to try and figure out if there's any truth at all to what's being referenced here. I've been close to people that were creating problems and tried to give them the benefit of the doubt if they were participating in accountability. In a couple of instances, decades ago, I discovered that this participation was not sincere, and I left the friendship. i've never knowingly defended anything like what's on that flyer.

I  have tried my whole life to help people around me to be safer, and to check myself and my own behavior.
I hope everyone from my past understands that if i've wronged them in any way i am available to hear that. The people around me do not consider me a danger to
them.
I don't know why someone would make something like that about me, and neither do any of the people in my life.
love to all and i understand everyone's concern.
-c

Twisted Teens have been experiencing a breakout year. In 2026, they've released three critically acclaimed albums, signed to Sub Pop Records, have been the subject of several big media profiles (including one at Pitchfork), and are currently on tour with Kurt Vile — hence the references to Sub Pop, Pitchfork, and Kurt Vile on the flyers.

entry.title: SOAK – “transmitter park”
entry.summary: Irish singer-songwriter Bridie Monds-Watson makes big-hearted and tender songs as SOAK. “transmitter park,” the latest single off their forthcoming album decembers (out, fittingly, on December 4), is an anthem for the cryers. Boy, do I love a good cry. But as cathartic as it can be to let the waterworks flow, it can also be…
entry.content:
Irish singer-songwriter Bridie Monds-Watson makes big-hearted and tender songs as SOAK. "transmitter park," the latest single off their forthcoming album decembers (out, fittingly, on December 4), is an anthem for the cryers. Boy, do I love a good cry. But as cathartic as it can be to let the waterworks flow, it can also be disconcerting. Like, why am I crying on the tube watching two old men shoot the shit or seeing the sun set on my way home? The latter is probably cause it's going down at 4 p.m., but alas, sometimes we cry and we don't know the cause. That's sort of how "transmitter park" came about.

Monds-Watson explained:

I was in New York with a lot of time to myself. I love setting a task when I’m lost in a city. My plan was to go to Levain and get a cookie. Afterwards, I went to Transmitter Park for the first time. It was nighttime, and looking out at Manhattan I found myself crying, and I just let myself cry. This song is about me trying to make sense of that. I’m someone who is trying to get better. My whole life, my process was to not break too easily, to be resilient. But the last few years, the voice issues, the autoimmune disease, my body has had a lot to grapple with. I think I collected all of those things, and it wasn’t until I was on my own in New York that I allowed myself to not push the feelings away. At that stage, I was getting better, and vocal rehab helped a lot. So I had some relief, and it just happened: breaking, coming fully undone.

"transmitter park" is built around crusty acoustic guitar strums and soft shaker percussion. And, it has one killer chorus: "When I break, I'll cry a great lake/ I know it's too late when I do/ Let that dam burst and a whole year's worth comes rushing through." Just in time for the one of the most emotional times of the year — the holidays.

Watch the video, by Monds-Watson and Molly McGuffin, below.

decembers is out 12/4 on Rough Trade. Pre-order it here.

entry.title: New Cap’n Jazz/Owls Offshoot caPn j’OWLS Announce Existence, Release Debut Album
entry.summary: We can now add one more band name to the Kinsella extended universe. Really, they’ve jammed two of the existing band names together. Tim Kinsella, his cousin Nate Kinsella, and Victor Villarreal have been playing in bands together forever. As Illinois teenagers in the ’90s, Tim Kinsella and Villarreal were in Cap’n Jazz, one of…
entry.content:
We can now add one more band name to the Kinsella extended universe. Really, they've jammed two of the existing band names together.

Tim Kinsella, his cousin Nate Kinsella, and Victor Villarreal have been playing in bands together forever. As Illinois teenagers in the '90s, Tim Kinsella and Villarreal were in Cap'n Jazz, one of the most beloved and influential emo bands to ever arise from the Midwest. Post-Y2K, with Cap'n Jazz member Davey von Bohlen off doing the Promise Ring, the rest of the group relaunched as Owls and made more essential underground rock music. Both Cap'n Jazz and Owls have reunited over the years, and the more recent Cap'n Jazz outings have also featured Nate Kinsella, a longtime fixture of the Kinsella extended universe who has played with Tim in Joan Of Arc and Make Believe and with Mike Kinsella in Lies and American Football.

That brings us to caPn j'OWLS, the newly formed trio of Tim, Nate, and Victor. As teased a few days ago, today the band has announced its existence and released its self-titled debut album. But to listen to it, you're going to have to buy a physical copy (from Polyvinyl, naturally). The caPn j'OWLS LP will not be on DSPs, which means no streaming, not even MP3s for sale. You want the record, you're going to have to buy a record.

As someone who was blessed with a rare and precious stream of this project, I can tell you that if you're part of Kinsella nation, you're going to want to own caPn j'OWLS. It finds the old pals in fine form, flexing their well-known proclivities for zany time signatures, unconventional chord progressions, and impassioned vocal delivery. But if this music is unmistakably the work of from the Cap'n Jazz braintrust, it's also seasoned with years of wisdom and experience, and this crew continues to push stylistic and compositional boundaries in intriguing ways.

Tim Kinsella and Victor Villarreal both have solo shows coming up — Kinsella playing Joan Of Arc songs at US gigs this week, Villarreal touring the UK next month — and caPn j'OWLS will be on sale at those. You can also order it online here. Check out those tour dates below.

entry.title: Tube Alloys Announce New Album Live From Death Row: Hear “Down By The Pool”
entry.summary: Live On Death Row, the upcoming sophomore album from LA post-punk band Tube Alloys, was not actually recorded live on death row. It’s not a Johnny Cash/Folsom Prison situation. Don’t get confused. For years, I thought that Rocket From The Crypt’s Live From Camp X-Ray was an actual live album. Don’t be like me and…
entry.content:
Live On Death Row, the upcoming sophomore album from LA post-punk band Tube Alloys, was not actually recorded live on death row. It's not a Johnny Cash/Folsom Prison situation. Don't get confused. For years, I thought that Rocket From The Crypt's Live From Camp X-Ray was an actual live album. Don't be like me and turn your brain off the second that you see the word "live" in an album title. This is just a regular studio album, OK? We good on that?

Australian transplant Jai Love started Tube Alloys during the pandemic, and the band showed a lot of spark with their 2023 debut album Magnetic Point and their 2024 two-song single "Evil Angels" b/w "Lizard Kingdom." Next year, they'll release Live From Death Row, and they've moved in a sharp, catchy direction on opening track "Down By The Pool." It's a brash, wiry stomper that finds Love fuming about "postmodern groups in pointy elf boots." I love a turn of phrase like that. The track has a sense of purposeful, hard-rockin' bounce, and I would recommend it to anyone who likes Spiritual Cramp.

Band member Baylee Barrett directed the "Down By The Pool" video, in which Jai Love wears a very wet black suit and runs around LA. In a press release, he says, "This was my audition tape for the new James Bond film. Obviously, I didn't get the part." Here's what Barrett says about it:

Today, we sludge around in a state of survival. It’s seeming harder to stay aware of ourselves and our surroundings. So desperate for connection we look for it in all the wrong places. So desperate for meaning we begin to attach meaning to everything. There was something really funny to us in the image of Jai soaking wet walking around the city. So we just got on and did it ourselves. It was even more funny that no one seemed to notice.

Check it out below.

entry.title: End It – “Pay To Cum” (Bad Brains Cover)
entry.summary: Bad Brains’ 1980 debut single “Pay To Cum” isn’t the first hardcore single, since Middle Class’ “Out Of Vogue” came out about a year earlier. But “Pay To Cum” set new benchmarks in speed and ferocity, and it’s hard to imagine a more influential underground song. Yesterday, Baltimore hardcore greats End It shared their own…
entry.content:
Bad Brains' 1980 debut single "Pay To Cum" isn't the first hardcore single, since Middle Class' "Out Of Vogue" came out about a year earlier. But "Pay To Cum" set new benchmarks in speed and ferocity, and it's hard to imagine a more influential underground song. Yesterday, Baltimore hardcore greats End It shared their own version of "Pay To Cum," slowing the song down just a touch and putting their own stamp on it.

Early next year, End It will release a new 7" with covers of two Bad Brains songs, "Pay To Cum" and its original B-side "Stay Close To Me." It'll be End It's first release since the whole bananaman situation earlier this year. This isn't End It's first time saluting their hardcore ancestors; last year, they included a version of Maximum Penalty's 1996 song "Could You Love Me?" on their debut album, Wrong Side Of Heaven. Check out their "Pay To Cum" cover and the Bad Brains original below.

The "Pay To Cum" b/w "Stay Close To Me" 7" is out 1/8 on Flatspot. Flatspot also recently announced a new coffee table book, Intent To Distribute, to celebrate the label's 20th anniversary.

entry.content:
Since releasing his underrated 2024 album Curve 1, British producer Mura Masa has been returning from time to time, with singles like "I'm Really Hot (For Myself)," "Jump," and, most recently, "Needja" featuring UK rapper Ledbyher, to remind us he knows how to consistently switch up his sound while owning the dance floor. This week, he's back again.

A few days ago Mura Masa emerged with another single, "Nobody Can Know Me Like You Do," which features several refreshing rhythm breaks and shifting beats. It presents to me as the more composed sister of "We Found Love"; there are shimmers of acoustic guitar towards the end. It's the kind of dance-pop song you want to sing and dance to in a sunshower. Listen below.

entry.title: Jonah Yano – “The Door”
entry.summary: Montreal/Japan musician Jonah Yano has shared the new single "The Door" off of his forthcoming album 'Spin.'
entry.content:
Montreal and Japan-based musician Jonah Yano previewed his new record Spin with two songs last month, sharing the title track and "Holding On" at once. Now we're getting a third, "The Door," which was co-written by Noah Williamson and features Chris Edmondson on saxophone and piano, Ben Maclean on pedal steel, Leighton Harrell on double bass, and Raiden Louie on drums. Yano explains:

"The Door" is definitely an outlier on the new record - I never set out to write or record an alt-country song but it kind of just ended up happening. Of all the songs on Spin, "The Door" was the song I felt the most unsure about releasing because it sounds and feels the least like me and all of my musical instincts but it's that friction between what this song is and the idea I have of myself that led me to keep it on the album and even share it as a single. It's really interesting to make songs that I have no business making and, in the instance of "The Door," it ended up being the song that I had the most fun recording, ever.

entry.title: Or Best Offer – “Feet Out”
entry.summary: Ahead of their upcoming album 'It Will Appear,' New York duo Or Best Offer have shared another new singled entitled "Feet Out."
entry.content:
Or Best Offer, the New York duo of Grace Schmidhauser and Brian Culligan, are putting out their new album It Will Appear in January. We posted lead single "Fast Strong Horse" a few weeks ago. They've followed that up with another new song called "Feet Out," a compellingly off-kilter indie-rock odyssey that repeatedly unravels and pulls itself back together over the course of its five-minute runtime.

"'Feet Out' is about trying to sift through dogma and platitudes to find truth, the awkwardness of learning to think and behave in the direction of growth, and experiences of collective care and forgiveness," Schmidhauser says. "Like a lot of this album, it’s about the attempt to transcend the self-obsession that shame can produce and the strange, slow crawl toward redemption." Listen below.

It Will Appear is out 1/15/2027. Pre-order here.

entry.title: Phoebe Bridgers – “Anything” (Adrianne Lenker Cover)
entry.summary: Phoebe Bridgers used to have an annual tradition. Every year, right around the holidays, she’d release a holiday cover. Some of those covers were Christmas songs, and some of them just had general Christmas vibes. entry.content:
Phoebe Bridgers used to have an annual tradition. Every year, right around the holidays, she'd release a holiday cover. Some of those covers were Christmas songs, and some of them just had general Christmas vibes. Bridgers seemingly abandoned that tradition after covering the Handsome Family's "So Much Wine" in 2022 and doing the traditional "The Parting Glass" with boygenius and Irish folk duo Ye Vagabonds in 2023. But now, Bridgers is bringing it back, sharing her version of an Adrianne Lenker song.

Big Thief leader Adrianne Lenker released "Anything" as the lead single from her 2020 album songs. Bridgers co-produced her version of the song with regular collaborators Jack Antonoff, Tony Berg, and Ethan Gruska, and her version samples Lenker's original. The single also calls back to Stranger In The Alps with Angela Deane's cover art. Bridgers and Lenker are both donating their proceeds from the single to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund. With her version, Bridgers keeps the lilting fragility of Lenker's original track, but her take is a lot lusher and more produced. Check out the cover and the original below.

Phoebe Bridgers obviously has a lot going on right now. Her Lost Weekend is up for Album Of The Year at the Grammys, and she just extended her no-phones arena tour and played SNL. She made her acting debut alongside our new James Bond in Lance Oppenheim's Primetime, and she released the end-credits song "On Video." That was her first new track since Lost Weekend came out, and this "Anything" cover is her second.

entry.title: Horse Vision Announce New Album Mouse: Hear “Proud Of Me”
entry.summary: Electronic-tinged indie rock duo Horse Vision have announced their new album 'Mouse' and shared its lead single, "Proud Of Me."
entry.content:
Another horse band has entered the chat. Johan Nilsson and Gabriel von Essen are Horse Vision, a Stockholm duo who specialize in an intriguingly warped, digital-native form of classic indie rock for the internet era.

After releasing their debut album Another Life last year, Horse Vision are back today with the announcement of its follow-up, Mouse, for their new label Scenic Route. They're also sharing lead single "Proud Of Me," which they describe as "a song about asking for things you really can't ask for." As they explain:

This track was written and recorded in our Spökhuset in Stockholm on June 4th, 2026. It’s a sparse and minimal production laced with naive melodies and riffs, referencing a musical past of small musical gestures and minimal ornamentation. The chorus was recorded and written a couple of years ago, but never made it to become a song until now.

Unless I'm mistaken, the track also features a sample of Navi's iconic "hey, listen!" sound effect from the original Ocarina Of Time, which just got a fancy new remake. Timely! Listen below and check out the dates for Horse Vision's upcoming headlining tour following the release of the record in February.

entry.title: Baby Wave – “Country Roads”
entry.summary: Nashville indie rock trio Baby Wave have shared their new single "Country Roads," which is not a John Denver cover.
entry.content:
Baby Wave announced their signing to Saddle Creek last month with the release of their single "The Scene Is Changing." Now, the Nashville indie-rock trio of multi-instrumentalists book NOT brooke, Gardner Gottsegen, and Jakob Bibb are back with another new song. It's called "Country Roads," and no, it is not a John Denver cover.

"We wrote 'Country Roads' when we were living in Athens, OH," Bibb explains. "We were into writing about college students when we first set foot in Athens, so that's who naturally popped up in this song. We accidentally ended up writing about how Gardner and I met Book, at a party when she was pretty hammered."

"The only lyrics I contributed to the verses were the dark ones," book continues. "Then I went upstairs and cried. Thank God I got out of the way, because Jake & Gardner struck gold. I developed the spoken word section and bridge through improvisation. I usually tell a different variation of the same story during our set, but sometimes I go off-script on a rant or infuse it with that week’s events."

"I remember us all laughing at the idea of bringing up 'Country Roads' by John Denver, but when we were done laughing, we had a real idea of what the song was about: being lost in a busy world and heading into the woods to find some solace and direction," Gottsegen adds. 

The track, which surges up into a beautifully crushing wave of distortion in the chorus, comes with a video filmed on Gottsegen's family farm in Vermont. "It was really special to be shown around Gardner’s stomping grounds for the first time while the cameras were rolling. He planned out all the locations in advance, and we got to just go along for the ride," Book recalls.

"We shot additional footage in the city - I think the dichotomy of the two settings conveys the same sense of yearning I feel in the song," Book says. "I went for that same feeling in the edit, which I did on tour with Annie DiRusso in Brazil." Watch and listen to below.

entry.title: Mei Semones – “Kira Kira”

We’ve posted the title track and “2 Hands.” Today, she shares “Kira Kira,” a bright and playful new track that toggles back and forth between…
entry.content:
The Brooklyn-based pan-genre traveler Mei Semones was a Stereogum Artist To Watch last year, and she's getting ready to follow her debut album Animaru with a new one called Howl. We've posted the title track and "2 Hands." Today, she shares "Kira Kira," a bright and playful new track that toggles back and forth between English and Japanese lyrics.

"Kira Kira" is a dizzy love song that captures a certain weightlessness. Semones gets in some flighty guitar heroics, which pair nicely with the track's flighty strings. In a press release, Semones says, "'Kira Kira' means 'sparkle sparkle,' and for this song I thought it would be fun to use different Japanese onomatopoeia throughout the lyrics, like 'koro koro, niko niko, pika pika, fuwa fuwa,' as I think those types of Japanese words are so cute and unique to the language." Check it out below.

Howl is out 1/15 on Verve/Interscope.

entry.title: Taylor Swift Returns To CMAs, Ella Langley Breaks Record For Most Wins In One Night
entry.summary: When Taylor Swift released her Toy Story 5 soundtrack song “I Knew It, I Knew You” earlier this year, it was explicitly marketed as Swift’s return to country music, the genre where she began her career. That track’s actual country qualities are debatable, but they were enough to get Swift back onstage at the Country…
entry.content:
When Taylor Swift released her Toy Story 5 soundtrack song "I Knew It, I Knew You" earlier this year, it was explicitly marketed as Swift's return to country music, the genre where she began her career. That track's actual country qualities are debatable, but they were enough to get Swift back onstage at the Country Music Association awards for the first time in many years.

The CMAs are country music's biggest annual awards show, and Swift used to be a regular there. This year's awards show went down on Wednesday night, and Swift gave her first CMAs performance in 13 years. (She also presented an award in 2016, so this was her first time back on the show in any capacity in a decade.) Swift performed "I Knew It, I Knew You," and she also worked in one chorus of her early smash "Our Song,." which just turned 20. Beyond that, she made sure that her performance had all sorts of nods to her past and to country music in general.

Naturally, Swift's performance was an elaborate production. She started it off in a dressing room full of her old costumes. As she wound her way through the backstage hallways at Nashville's Bridgestone Arena, lots of country stars made cameos: Brad Paisley, Little Big Town, Sugarland, Brooks & Dunn, Lainey Wiilson, Eric Church. When she came out onto a stage made to look like the tree from Toy Story 5, her onetime tourmate Keith Urban joined her on banjo. There are already TikToks breaking down all the references in the performance, which you can watch below.

Swift also presented the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award to Brook & Dunn, who got a tribute performance from Halestorm, Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, HARDY, and Marcus King and won Vocal Duo Of The Year for the 17th time. "I Knew It, I Knew You" won a Hollywood Music In Media Award, and Swift accepted that one in a pre-recorded video.

But Taylor Swift wasn't the night's big winner. Instead, that distinction went to Ella Langley, the latest singer to break out of country music and dominate the pop charts. Langley set a new record for most CMA. Langley won six awards, including Entertainer, Album, and Song Of The Year. One of the people who Langley defeated was Taylor Swift, as her record-setting smash "Choosin' Texas" beat "I Knew It, I Knew You" for Single Of The Year.

Before Langley shattered the record, the most CMAs that anyone had ever won in a single night was five, and that record was jointly held by Johnny Cash in 1969, Vince Gill in 1993, Alan Jackson in 2002, and Lainey Wilson in 2023. At 27, Langley became the second-youngest Entertainer Of The Year winner ever. (Taylor Swift was 19 when she won it in 2009.) "Choosin' Texas" is currently America's #1 song for a 28th fucking week.

During the telecast, Langley and Miranda Lambert performed their new duet "Snakeskin Boots." Lambert co-wrote "Choosin' Texas," and she co-produced that song, as well as every other track on Langley's blockbuster Dandelion.

Lambert and her onetime adversary Kacey Musgraves also sang their recent collab "Horses And Divorces."

The suddenly omnipresent 47-year-old breakout star Stephen Wilson Jr. won Best New Artist, and he performed his new single "I'm A Song" with Chris Stapleton. On last night's Jimmy Kimmel Live!, Wilson also sang a different song, "Exorcisms On The Weekend." Presumably, the Kimmel performance was pre-recorded.

Stapleton also did double duty, joining notable non-country act Mumford & Sons for their song "Here."

Lainey Wilson hosted the show, and she performed her new song "Just A Woman," which was released right before the broadcast.

The show opened with Wilson and Vince Gill singing "I Will Always Love You" in tribute to the late Dolly Parton.

Later in the show, Zach Top and Dierks Bentley also paid tribute to the late John Anderson, covering his 1983 song "Swingin'."

A bunch of these people will presumably show up for cameos in The Comeback King, the new Judd Apatow movie where Glen Powell plays a country star who's trying to return from a period of career wilderness. The trailer came out yesterday, presumably to cash in on any attention that the CMAs got. It looks pretty bad!

entry.title: Mythless Announce Debut Album Hex: Hear “Brocken Spectre”
entry.summary: Mythless, the duo of two former Fang Island members, have announced their debut album 'Hex' and shared lead single "Brocken Spectre."
entry.content:
Mythless is the progressive rock duo made up of two former Fang Island members, guitarist/vocalist Jason Bartell and drummer Marc St. Saveur. They've technically been around for a while now, but after a couple of EPs in 2018 and 2022 (and a big Fang Island discography box set in 2024), Mythless are finally getting around to coming out with their debut album.

That album, Hex, is both a meditation on Bartell's past, life, and career and a love letter to the endless possibilities of his favorite instrument: the electric guitar. "That's who I am, that’s what comes out when I sit down and play guitar and that’s not gonna change," he says. "I don't play acoustic guitar. I'm not good enough to play acoustic guitar. It needs to be distorted and loud."

Alongside the album announcement, Mythless are sharing lead single "Brocken Spectre." Named after the optical phenomenon in which an observer's shadow is cast, magnified and haloed, into the air, it's a maximalist anthem that approaches a kind of ecclesiastical splendor with its layers of electric guitar and vocal harmonies. Hear it below.

Hex is out 1/29 on Joyful Noise.

entry.title: Macklemore Shares “Where’s Our Love,” Benefitting Mothers And Children Of Gaza
entry.summary: Macklemore has been vociferously supporting the Palestinian people for years now, and he escalated his efforts in recent months. Sheeran’s other opening acts…
entry.content:
Macklemore has been vociferously supporting the Palestinian people for years now, and he escalated his efforts in recent months. After causing a stir by calling for a free Palestine while opening some Ed Sheeran stadium shows on Labor Day weekend, he was dropped from the tour, sparking an even bigger controversy. Sheeran's other opening acts and backing band backed out in protest, while Macklemore donated $1 million in tour proceeds to Palestinian aid organizations and announced his Free Palestine Tour. The tour is underway overseas, but Macklemore says US arenas aren't willing to host it.

Now comes his latest song in support of the cause. New single "Where's Our Love" is a benefit for the Mother Of Hind Fund, which supports mothers and children in Gaza. The track will be on streaming services Friday, but it's on Macklemore's Instagram now in music video form. Check it out below.

"Where's Our Love" follows prior protest singles "Hind's Hall" and "Hind's Hall 2," both named for Hind Rajab, a six-year-old Palestinian girl who was killed alongside her family in Gaza, and the Columbia University student protestors who commandeered Hamilton Hall and renamed it in Hind's honor.
